rules.name: Convex set segment criterion
rules.input_form: set C
rules.output_form: all line segments between points of C remain in C
preconditions: The ambient vector space is fixed
rules.operation: Classify a set as convex by its segment closure property.
examples: Intervals and Euclidean balls are standard convex sets
counterexamples: Sets with missing interior gaps along connecting segments are not convex

rules.name: First-order necessary condition for unconstrained optima
rules.input_form: differentiable objective with interior local extremum x_*
preconditions: x_* is an interior point and f is differentiable there
rules.operation: Use vanishing gradient as a necessary condition for interior local extrema.
examples: Stationary points are necessary candidates for smooth interior optima
counterexamples: Boundary optima need not satisfy the interior gradient-zero condition

rules.name: Gradient descent update rule
rules.input_form: x_k and gradient of f at x_k
preconditions: A positive step size alpha_k is specified
rules.operation: Update an iterate by moving opposite the gradient to seek descent.
examples: Moving opposite the gradient gives a local descent direction for smooth objectives
counterexamples: Stepping along the positive gradient is invalid as a descent update for minimization

rules.name: Lagrange multiplier rule
rules.input_form: objective f and equality constraint g(x) = 0
preconditions: The standard differentiability and regularity hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Relate objective and constraint gradients at constrained extrema.
examples: Equality-constrained optimization introduces multiplier equations coupling objective and constraint gradients
counterexamples: Applying the rule when the constraint gradient vanishes everywhere is invalid in general

rules.name: Weak duality seed for minimization
rules.input_form: primal-feasible and dual-feasible values
preconditions: The primal-dual pair is formed in a standard minimization framework
rules.operation: Lower-bound primal minimization values by dual-feasible certificates.
examples: Dual certificates provide guaranteed lower bounds on primal objective values
counterexamples: Reversing the inequality without strong-duality hypotheses is invalid

rules.name: Subgradient inequality rule
rules.input_form: convex function f, point x, candidate subgradient g
preconditions: f is convex on the active domain
rules.operation: Use a subgradient as a global supporting linear functional for a convex objective.
examples: Nondifferentiable convex optimization still admits first-order support inequalities through subgradients
counterexamples: Using a local slope that violates the global support inequality is invalid

rules.name: Jensen inequality seed
rules.input_form: convex function and convex combination
rules.output_form: f(sum lambda_i x_i) <= sum lambda_i f(x_i)
preconditions: Weights form a convex combination and f is convex
rules.operation: Control the function value of an average by the average of function values for convex objectives.
examples: Convexity controls objective values under averaging and mixture formation
counterexamples: Reversing the inequality for convex functions is invalid

rules.name: KKT condition seed
rules.input_form: nonlinear program with equality and inequality constraints
preconditions: The standard differentiability and constraint-qualification hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Use KKT relations as first-order necessary conditions for constrained optimality.
examples: KKT conditions generalize Lagrange multipliers to inequality-constrained problems
counterexamples: Applying KKT without the needed qualification hypotheses is invalid in general

rules.name: Complementary slackness rule
rules.input_form: inequality constraint slack and multiplier
preconditions: The KKT framework is active
rules.operation: Couple multipliers and inactive constraint slack through zero products.
examples: Active constraints may carry positive multipliers, while inactive constraints force zero multipliers in the basic complementary-slackness picture
counterexamples: Assigning positive multiplier and positive slack simultaneously is invalid in the standard KKT relation

rules.name: Strong duality seed in convex optimization
rules.input_form: convex primal-dual pair
rules.output_form: equal optimal values under standard qualification hypotheses
preconditions: The problem is convex and satisfies a standard duality qualification hypothesis
rules.operation: Close the duality gap under standard convex-optimization regularity assumptions.
examples: Convex programs with suitable constraint qualifications can close the duality gap
counterexamples: Promoting weak duality to equality without the extra hypotheses is invalid
